name: Storm & Stress
label: Touch and Go
lede: Ian Williams wanted a band that was Don Caballero turned upside down, so he found a free-jazz drummer at a party, played quietly through a full stack of amps, and made two records nobody could count along to.

eras.title: Don Caballero, upside down
eras.text: Ian Williams was the second guitarist in Don Caballero, Pittsburgh's tightly drilled instrumental band, and he wasn't happy there. Storm & Stress, named for the German literary movement Sturm und Drang, was built to be its opposite.

years.src: Scaruffi: Ian Williams interview · Wikipedia: Storm & Stress
years.h: Williams hears Kevin Shea's terrible band at a party
years.p: A friend warned him off the improv outfit fortystories. Within a minute of drummer [[Kevin Shea|3dcceeae-023b-4a6a-a770-0b260f099019]] starting, Williams said, he thought about music differently.
years.xp:
Fortystories was Shea's group with pianist and singer Micah Gaugh. Williams, Shea and bassist George Draguns started playing as Storm & Stress in 1994.

What Williams wanted, he told Piero Scaruffi in 1999: "a band upside down from Don Cab." That meant playing quietly through a full stack of amps and "never knowing what the time signature was."

years.h: First shows: Pittsburgh dives, and the amps in front of the band
years.p: Early sets in working-class bars were concept shows, some without music. At the first one people came to see, the band stood behind its amps and couldn't hear itself.
years.xp: "Just trying to frustrate people," Williams said of those early shows, then corrected himself: they weren't trying to, it just always seemed to happen. He said Storm & Stress didn't play a real show until Don Caballero stopped playing.

years.h: Storm & Stress riffs end up on Don Caballero 2
years.p: Don Caballero was making a record and Storm & Stress was still in what Williams called its laboratory phase, so some of its riffs went to the other band.

eras.title: Fifty-nine minutes with Albini
eras.text: To make a record the band had to fix things that were never meant to be fixed. It turned the improvisations into what Williams insisted were songs and took them to Steve Albini.

years.src: Wikipedia: Storm & Stress · Storm & Stress band bio
years.h: Eric Emm replaces George Draguns on bass
years.p: [[Eric Emm|416157a8-24fa-4851-b9ee-e4fd7b945025]], credited on the Pittsburgh band bio as M. Eric Topolsky, plays bass on the first album.

years.src: Storm & Stress band bio · Wikipedia: Storm & Stress (album)
years.h: Seven songs, 59 minutes, and a pause for Micah Gaugh
years.p: Albini records the debut at Chicago Recording Co. for Touch and Go. Gaugh sings and plays piano on "Micah Gaugh Sings All Is All".
years.xp:
The band bio describes the sound as "rock without a beat", and Williams insisted it was composed: "We wrote things we called songs." He compared it to a Don Cab song seen with your eyes blurred, so only rough fuzzy shapes remain.

The sleeve photos were shot inside a rapidly decelerating truck. Entertainment Weekly gave the record a B+.
play: We Write Threnodies. We Write with Explosions

years.cap: Flyer for the record release show, Brew House Space 101, Pittsburgh, August 16, 1997
years.h: Record release night at the Brew House on the South Side
years.p: The debut gets its Pittsburgh launch at Brew House Space 101, with shows in Washington, D.C. and elsewhere to follow.

eras.title: O'Rourke, then the end
eras.text: By 1999 Williams lived in Chicago and Shea in New York. They made a second, shorter record with Jim O'Rourke at Electrical Audio, and when it came out in 2000 Williams was finished with both of his Pittsburgh bands.

years.src: Scaruffi: Ian Williams interview · Wikipedia: Under Thunder and Fluorescent Lights
years.h: Jim O'Rourke records the second album at Electrical Audio
years.p: Sessions run through June and July in Chicago. Williams picked O'Rourke because he wouldn't decide the music was esoteric and back out of the process.
years.xp: Williams compared his two engineers for Scaruffi: Albini treated the signal on tape as the song itself, while O'Rourke heard a hidden secret in each track that had to be drawn out by a particular mix. He said he didn't see either approach as right or wrong.

years.cap: Storm & Stress on stage in Newcastle, UK, 2000
years.src: Wikipedia: Under Thunder and Fluorescent Lights
years.h: Under Thunder and Fluorescent Lights, the long titles intact
years.p: Nine tracks in 43 minutes, with drummer Jim Black and Gaugh as guests. Pitchfork gave it 7.8.
play: The Sky's the Ground, the Bombs Are Plants, and We're the Sun, Love

years.h: Williams shops for records in High Fidelity
years.p: He has a cameo as a customer in the record store, just after John Cusack's character announces he'll sell five copies of the Beta Band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Storm & Stress · Wikipedia: Ian Williams
years.h: Storm & Stress and Don Caballero both end for Williams
years.p: Storm & Stress is done after two albums and US and European tours. Williams's run in Don Caballero, which began in 1992, also ends in 2000.

eras.title: Battles, Tanlines, Talibam!
eras.text: The three went separate ways and all kept working. A bit of the old name came back in 2014.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ian Williams · Wikipedia: Storm & Stress · Wikipedia: Kevin Shea
years.h: Williams moves to New York and forms Battles
years.p: [[Battles|8522b9b6-b295-48d7-9a10-8618fb80beb8]] keeps his one-handed tapping and adds keyboards in the other hand. [[Eric Emm|416157a8-24fa-4851-b9ee-e4fd7b945025]] later sings and plays guitar in Tanlines, and [[Kevin Shea|3dcceeae-023b-4a6a-a770-0b260f099019]] becomes a fixture of New York free jazz with Talibam! and Mostly Other People Do the Killing.

years.h: Shea and Draguns reunite as Form and Mess
years.p: With guitarist Nick Millevoi, the original rhythm section releases an album under a name that tips its hat to the old band.
